newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Earthquake shakes Croatian coast near Dubrovnik.
newsitem.headline: Earthquake shakes Croatian coast near Dubrovnik.

text.p: An earthquake measuring nearly 6.0 on the Richter scale shook the Croatian coast near the tourist resort of Dubrovnik on Thursday night, but there were no initial reports of casualties or damage.
John Minsch, seismologist at U.S. Geological Survey's National Earthquake Information Center in Golden, Colorado, said the quake hit at 10.44 p.m. local time (2044 GMT).
He pinpointed its epicentre at latitude 42.85 degrees north, longitude 17.90 east, or about 15 miles (24 km) northwest of Dubrovnik.

"It was felt through a wide area," he said. "It hit 15 miles northwest of Dubrovnik right near the shore." He said the preliminary magnitude was 5.9 on the Richter scale, and the depth was shallow, which increases the likelihood of causing damage on the surface.
A receptionist at the Hotel Lapad in Dubrovnik said guests were frightened by the size of the tremor.
"People were panicking and running out of the building but everyone is begining to calm down now," he told Reuters by telephone.
The tremor could be felt 400 km (250 miles) to the north in Zagreb and in the Bosnian capital Sarajevo.
